[4] ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.﴾

[5] ﴿Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you and turn away, because you are a people who exceed the limits?﴾

﴿Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you and turn away, because you are a people who exceed the limits?﴾ That is: Shall We neglect you and turn the Reminder away from you because of your excess? [11] ﴿And He who sends down from the sky water in measure, and We revive thereby a dead land. Thus will you be brought forth.﴾

﴿And He who sends down from the sky water in measure﴾ means: in the amount needed for it. The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12–14] ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that. ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾ means: He created everything and made it in pairs, so that from it He made the male and the female. ﴿And made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾ means: of the boats and beasts, those which you ride. ﴿That you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 13]. **The discussion on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[15] ﴿And they have attributed to Him, from among His servants, a portion. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful.﴾

﴿And they have attributed to Him, from among His servants, a portion﴾: that is, these polytheists assigned to God a share of His creation, and this is their saying about the angels: "they are the daughters of God." Al-Qashani said: That is, they acknowledged that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, their originator and their Initiator. Yet they anthropomorphized Him and divided Him by affirming a child for Him, which is part of the parent and similar to him in kind, because they are apparent, corporeal people who do not go beyond the level of sense and imagination, and who do not strip themselves of the garments of corporeal things, so they cannot perceive abstract realities or sacred essences, let alone the Essence of God, Exalted is He. Thus, whatever they conceived and imagined was something corporeal. For this reason they denied the prophets regarding the affirmation of the Hereafter, the Resurrection, the Gathering, and everything related to the Return, since their perception does not extend beyond the present life, and their minds, veiled from the light of guidance, reach only the affairs of livelihood. There is no fundamental affinity between their essences and the essences of the prophets, except in the outward aspect of humanity, so there is no need for anything beyond that. End of quotation.

﴿Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾: that is, extremely ingratiating in denying the blessings of their Lord which He bestowed upon them, and their ingratitude becomes evident to whoever reflects upon their condition.

[p-5261]

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16]

﴿Or has He taken daughters out of what He creates, and chosen sons for you?﴾

That is: rather, has He taken [daughters]? The *الهمزة* (al-hamza, the interrogative particle) here is for denunciation, to show their ignorance and to express wonder at their state, in that they were not content to attribute to God a part of His servants, to the point that they made that part the worse of the two parts, namely females rather than males. Moreover, they are the creatures of God most averse to females and most loathing of them, and their loathing reached the point that they buried them alive. It is as if it were said: suppose that ascribing offspring to Him is permissible, as a hypothesis and an illustration. Are you not ashamed of the injustice in the division, and of your claim that He preferred you over Himself with the better and higher of the two parts, leaving Himself the worse and lower of them?

So said al-Zamakhshari.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[17] ﴿When one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed grief.﴾

﴿When one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾, i.e., of daughters: ﴿his face becomes darkened﴾, i.e., from sorrow, distress and grief: ﴿and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾, i.e., his heart is filled with anguish.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verse 18:

(p-5262) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in disputation, is not clear (in expression)?﴾

﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments?﴾ That is: one who is raised in adornment, meaning daughters. ﴿And who, in disputation﴾ — that is, in argument — ﴿is not clear﴾ — that is, to whoever disputes with him by way of proof and evidence, because of his weakness and feebleness. The meaning is: Do you attribute to Allah, as a part of His creation, one who is such, and claim that he is a share of them?

Notice (tanbih):

Al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: In it is evidence for the permissibility of ornaments (huli, jewelry) for women. Abu al-'Aliyah was asked about gold for women, and he saw no harm in it, and he recited this verse.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾

﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾ That is: they made the angels of Allah, who are in His presence, glorifying Him and sanctifying Him, into females, and they said: ﴿they are daughters of Allah﴾. This was out of their ignorance of the right of Allah, glorified is He, and out of their audacity in uttering falsehood.

Al-Qashani said: When they heard from their predecessors the saying of the early sages concerning the affirmation of the angelic souls, and their being called feminine, either in consideration of the word (al-nufus, which is feminine in grammatical gender) or in consideration of their being affected and acted upon by the holy intellectual spirits, together with their description as being close to the Divine Presence, they imagined their femininity in reality, which is opposite to masculinity in animals, while being specially associated with Allah. So they made them daughters. The common folk rarely conceive of them except as subtle human forms of utmost beauty. End of quotation.

﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ That is: were they present at the creation of them by Allah, so that they describe them thus because of their knowledge of them and their seeing them? This is a rebuke to them and a mockery of them. ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾ That is: against them, the angels being declared free of what they attribute to them. ﴿And they will be questioned﴾ That is: about it on the Day of Resurrection, so that they bring proof of its truth, and they will find no way to that. In this is a warning of what it contains; for its recording and the questioning about it entail punishment and requital for it, and this is what is intended.

**On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[20, 21] ﴿And they say: "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess.﴾ ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21].

This is an explanation of another form of their misguidance, in their disputing, contending, and obstinacy. The Mu'tazilah (a theological school that held that God does not will evil or disobedience) used the apparent meaning of the verse to argue that God does not will evil and acts of disobedience. The People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah, the mainstream orthodox school) interpreted the verse in a way that accords with the sound creed, which is the generality of His will over everything, a principle stated in more than one verse. Since this verse and its counterparts have been battlegrounds of opinion, past and present, I have chosen to transcribe here what the verifying exegetes have said, following my practice of gathering the precious points of earlier scholars and adorning my works with them. So I say:

Al-Qashani (a Sufi exegete) said: When they heard from the prophets the linking of things to the will of God, the Exalted, they seized upon it and made it a pretext for denial. They said this not out of knowledge and certainty, but out of stubbornness and a wish to silence. For this reason God, the Exalted, refuted them with His words: ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, for had they known it, they would have been monotheists, attributing influence only to God. They would then have had no choice but to worship Him alone, since they would not see any benefit or harm in other than Him. ﴿They merely guess﴾: because by their deeds they contradicted their own words in this statement, when they magnified them and feared them, and frightened their prophets with their violence, as the people of Hud said: ﴿We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54]. When they threatened Abraham, peace be upon him, with their scheming, he replied with his words: ﴿I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something﴾ [al-An'am: 80], up to his words: ﴿How should I fear what you have associated?﴾ [al-An'am: 81]. End of quotation.

In al-Baydawi (a major Shafi'i exegesis) and its supercommentaries: This statement is an argument from them against the prohibition of worshipping other than God, or for its goodness. They mean that their worship of the angels is by His will, the Exalted. Therefore it would be commanded or good, and it is impossible for it to be forbidden or ugly. This argument is false, because will does not entail command or goodness, since will is the preponderance of some possibilities over others, whether good or ugly. That is why He called them ignorant in this argument. The summary is that the denial is directed at their making that a proof against the prohibition of their worship or for its goodness, not at the statement itself, which is a word of truth used to convey falsehood. End of quotation.

Al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munir, author of al-Intisaf) said in al-Intisaf: We, the company of the People of the Sunnah, say that everything is by His will, the Exalted, including misguidance and guidance, following the proof of reason and confirming the explicit text, such as His words: ﴿He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Nahl: 93]. This verse of al-Zukhruf only adds to this sound belief groundwork and makes it firmer and more correct. So we say: when the unbeliever says, "Had God willed, I would not have disbelieved," this is a word of truth by which he intends falsehood. That it is a word of truth is because of what we have laid down. That he intends falsehood is because the unbeliever's aim in this is to have a proof against God, imagining that from God's will regarding the misguidance of whoever is misguided it follows that He would not punish him for it, since he is doing what His will requires.

Then he said: Once what we have said is clear, God only refuted their claim because they imagined it was a proof against God. So God overturned their argument, refuted their hope, and showed that their claim stems from a false assumption and pure conjecture. He said: ﴿They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess﴾ and ﴿They merely suppose﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]. The sister verse of this one has made this interpretation explicit, namely His words, may He be exalted, in Surat al-An'am: ﴿Those who associated will say: "Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our might. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you could bring out for us? You follow only conjecture, and you do nothing but guess."﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. (p-5265) Here God shows that what drove these people to deny the messengers and to associate others with God was their delusion that they had a proof against God in their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. So He likened their state in relying on this illusion to the state of their predecessors. Then He showed that it is a belief arising from a deceptive assumption and a lying imagination, saying: ﴿You follow only conjecture, and you do nothing but guess﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. Then, when He had invalidated their claim to have a proof against God, He established God's proof against them by their words: ﴿Then God's is the conclusive proof﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. He then made clear that the refutation of them lies only in their using this to argue against God, not because the statement in itself is false. So He said: ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. This is the meaning of their words: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148], since the particle {law} (if/had) by its nature implies the impossibility of guidance because of the impossibility of will. The last verse indicates that God did not will their guidance, but willed their misguidance. Had He willed their guidance, they would not have gone astray. This is the upright religion, the straight path, the shining light, and the clear way. What refutes the argument of these people, while holding that God willed their misguidance, is that God made for the servant a capacity and facility for guidance and other things, among the acquired actions (kasbiyyah), so that the actions proceeding from him became the basis of responsibility, since they are voluntary, and one necessarily distinguishes them from compelled accidents. This verse establishes the proof and makes clear to those whom God has chosen the right path to sound beliefs. Since it is a subtle distinction that does not fit into the thinking of the dull, their understanding scattered and their thoughts changed. A group of the Qadariyyah (who affirmed human free will against divine decree) exaggerated and believed that the servant does whatever he wills against the will of his Lord, while the Jabriyyah (who denied human agency) went too far, believing that the servant has no power or choice at all and that all actions proceed from him by compulsion. As for the People of Truth, God granted them a portion of His guidance (p-5266) and guided them to the middle path. They followed the paths of peace and walked with the guide of success being their imam, illuminated by the lights of minds that point to the fact that all beings are by God's power and will. It did not escape their understanding that some actions may be within the servant's capacity, since they found by necessity a distinction between voluntary and compelled acts. But this is a capacity that accompanies the act without influence, and they distinguish between the necessary and the voluntary in conception. This is the verification, and God is the bestower of success. End of quotation.

Earlier, in the commentary on the verse of [al-An'am], many quotations from the imams were given on this verse at length, so refer to them if you wish.

As for His words: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21], that is, before this Qur'an, ﴿so that they hold fast to it﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21], that is, they act upon it, follow what is in it, and argue with it against you, like His words in another verse: ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you could bring out for us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 148], meaning by knowledge a revealed book concerning that.

They mean that their worship of the angels is by His will, the Exalted. Therefore it would be commanded or good, and it is impossible for it to be forbidden or ugly. This argument is false, because will does not entail command or goodness, since will is the preponderance of some possibilities over others, whether good or ugly. That is why He called them ignorant in this argument. The summary is that the denial is directed at their making that a proof against the prohibition of their worship or for its goodness, not at the statement itself, which is a word of truth used to convey falsehood. End of quotation.

Al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munir, author of al-Intisaf) said in al-Intisaf: We, the company of the People of the Sunnah, say that everything is by His will, the Exalted, including misguidance and guidance, following the proof of reason and confirming the explicit text, such as His words: ﴿He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Nahl: 93]. This verse of al-Zukhruf only adds to this sound belief groundwork and makes it firmer and more correct. So we say: when the unbeliever says, "Had God willed, I would not have disbelieved," this is a word of truth by which he intends falsehood. That it is a word of truth is because of what we have laid down. That he intends falsehood is because the unbeliever's aim in this is to have a proof against God, imagining that from God's will regarding the misguidance of whoever is misguided it follows that He would not punish him for it, since he is doing what His will requires.

Then he said: Once what we have said is clear, God only refuted their claim because they imagined it was a proof against God. So God overturned their argument, refuted their hope, and showed that their claim stems from a false assumption and pure conjecture. He said: ﴿They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess﴾ and ﴿They merely suppose﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]. The sister verse of this one has made this interpretation explicit, namely His words, may He be exalted, in Surat al-An'am: ﴿Those who associated will say: "Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our might. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you could bring out for us? You follow only conjecture, and you do nothing but guess."﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. (p-5265) Here God shows that what drove these people to deny the messengers and to associate others with God was their delusion that they had a proof against God in their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. So He likened their state in relying on this illusion to the state of their predecessors. Then He showed that it is a belief arising from a deceptive assumption and a lying imagination, saying: ﴿You follow only conjecture, and you do nothing but guess﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. Then, when He had invalidated their claim to have a proof against God, He established God's proof against them by their words: ﴿Then God's is the conclusive proof﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. He then made clear that the refutation of them lies only in their using this to argue against God, not because the statement in itself is false. So He said: ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. This is the meaning of their words: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148], since the particle {law} (if/had) by its nature implies the impossibility of guidance because of the impossibility of will. The last verse indicates that God did not will their guidance, but willed their misguidance. Had He willed their guidance, they would not have gone astray. This is the upright religion, the straight path, the shining light, and the clear way. What refutes the argument of these people, while holding that God willed their misguidance, is that God made for the servant a capacity and facility for guidance and other things, among the acquired actions (kasbiyyah), so that the actions proceeding from him became the basis of responsibility, since they are voluntary, and one necessarily distinguishes them from compelled accidents. This verse establishes the proof and makes clear to those whom God has chosen the right path to sound beliefs. Since it is a subtle distinction that does not fit into the thinking of the dull, their understanding scattered and their thoughts changed. A group of the Qadariyyah (who affirmed human free will against divine decree) exaggerated and believed that the servant does whatever he wills against the will of his Lord, while the Jabriyyah (who denied human agency) went too far, believing that the servant has no power or choice at all and that all actions proceed from him by compulsion. As for the People of Truth, God granted them a portion of His guidance (p-5266) and guided them to the middle path. They followed the paths of peace and walked with the guide of success being their imam, illuminated by the lights of minds that point to the fact that all beings are by God's power and will. It did not escape their understanding that some actions may be within the servant's capacity, since they found by necessity a distinction between voluntary and compelled acts. But this is a capacity that accompanies the act without influence, and they distinguish between the necessary and the voluntary in conception. This is the verification, and God is the bestower of success. End of quotation.

Earlier, in the commentary on the verse of [al-An'am], many quotations from the imams were given on this verse at length, so refer to them if you wish.

As for His words: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21], that is, before this Qur'an, ﴿so that they hold fast to it﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 21], that is, they act upon it, follow what is in it, and argue with it against you, like His words in another verse: ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you could bring out for us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 148], meaning by knowledge a revealed book concerning that.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Nay, they said: "We found our fathers following a certain religious community, and we are guided upon their footsteps."﴾

﴿Nay, they said: "We found our fathers following a certain religious community, and we are guided upon their footsteps."﴾ That is: they have no proof except the blind imitation (taqlid) of their fathers, who were ignorant like them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verse 23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾

﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ That is: just as these polytheists resorted to defending their proof by blind imitation (taqlid), so did those before them among the people of disbelief in Allah.

The judge (al-Qadi) said: In this there is consolation for him (ﷺ), and an indication that imitation in matters of this kind is an ancient error, and that those who imitate them likewise had no examined foundation. The singling out of the affluent (mutrafun) indicates that their comforts and love of idleness diverted them from reflection to imitation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verse 24:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something better guided than what you found your fathers following?" They said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾

﴿He said﴾ and it has been read: "Say" (qul): ﴿"Even if I bring you something better guided than what you found your fathers following?" They said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ That is: deniers, rejecters. And even if it were better guided (ahda), it is a despairing of the warner (lil-nadhir) that they should look into it or reflect upon it.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿So We took vengeance upon them; then see how was the end of the deniers.﴾

﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾ — that is, with the punishment of annihilation. ﴿Then see how was the end of the deniers﴾ — that is, the final outcome of their affair, which became an example and a lesson.

The discussion of the words of His saying, may He be exalted:

[26] ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship."﴾

﴿And when Abraham said﴾ Al-Qadi said: That is, remember the time of his saying this, so that they may see how he disassociated himself from blind imitation (taqlid) and held fast to proof; or so that they might follow him, if they had no alternative to imitation, for he was the most honorable of their forefathers. ﴿to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship."﴾ That is: I am free from your worship or from what you worship.

As for ﴿barā'﴾, with a fatha on the bā' (the ب), as is the reading of the majority, it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) like ṭalāq and ʿatāq, and it is intended in the sense of an adjective for emphasis (mubālaghah). Therefore it is applied to the singular and to other than the singular. It has also been read with a ḍamma on the bā', and then it is a single noun functioning as an intensive adjective (ṣifat mubālaghah), like ṭiwāl and kirām, with a ḍamma on the ṭā' and the kāf. And His saying:

(p-5268) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Except He who created me, for He will guide me.﴾

﴿Except He who created me﴾ is either an exception of disjunction (istithna' munqati') or of connection (istithna' muttasil), on the basis that "ma" (what) encompasses those in authority and others, and that they used to worship Allah and idols. Or "illa" (except) carries the sense of "ghayr" (other than), functioning as an attribute of "ma"; that is: I am free of the gods you worship, other than He who created me, i.e., brought me into being. ﴿For He will guide me﴾, i.e., to the true religion and to following the path of right guidance. The "sin" (sa) may be for emphasis (li-l-ta'kid), and this is supported by the verse in al-Shu'ara': ﴿He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 78] without it. The narrative is one and the same, and the present tense in both places is for continuity (li-l-istimrar). Or it may be for deferment and futurity (li-l-taswif wa-l-istiqbal), and the intended meaning is an additional guidance beyond what he had previously. Thus what is in the two verses differs in the reported speech or the reported matter, based on the repetition of his story.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[28] ﴿And He made it a word that remains in his descendants, so that they might return.﴾

﴿And He made it﴾ — that is, the testimony of tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness). ﴿A word that remains in his descendants﴾ — that is, enjoined upon them, inherited, transmitted, and preserved. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, and so did Jacob﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132]. ﴿So that they might return﴾ — that is, in order that they might return to His worship and turn to His oneness in all their affairs; or perhaps whoever among them had associated partners would return through the supplication of those among them who professed God's oneness.

Discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a manifest messenger.﴾

﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these people﴾: meaning the people of Makkah. ﴿And their fathers﴾: that is, those before them, in life; so I did not hasten to punish them for their disbelief. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾: that is, the call to monotheism (tawhid), or the Qur'an. ﴿And a manifest messenger﴾: that is, one whose mission is clear through the signs and proofs with which he argues against them in his claim to prophethood.

(p-٥٢٦٩) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾

﴿And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾ That is: they were deniers, obstinate. So they increased in their misguidance, adding to their polytheism the stubborn opposition to the truth.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[31] ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ That is, from one of the two: Makkah and al-Ta'if. The definite article (in al-qaryatayn, "the two cities") is for a known reference. ﴿Of importance﴾ means in rank and wealth, for prophethood is a great office that, in their estimation, befits none but a great man. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: They did not know that it is a spiritual rank, which requires greatness of soul through adorning oneself with virtues and holy perfections, not through embellishing oneself with worldly ornaments.

And His saying, may He be exalted:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[32] ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? It is We who apportion among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We raise some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾

﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ This is a rebuke, containing a denunciation and an expression of wonder at their presuming to dispose of what only He, the Exalted, has charge over. By "mercy" is meant prophethood. ﴿It is We who apportion among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾, i.e., We made some of them rich and some of them poor. ﴿And We raise some of them﴾, i.e., through wealth, ﴿above others in degrees, so that some of them﴾, meaning the rich, ﴿may take others﴾, meaning the poor, ﴿in service﴾, i.e., employed in labour, and in what sustains livelihoods and reaches what benefits. This is not due to any perfection in the one who is granted abundance, nor to any deficiency in the one who is kept in straitened circumstances; rather, it is for the need of mutual support and cohesion, by which their community is held together. As for the divine breezes and the God-given knowledge (al-'ulum al-ladunniyya), these do not require abundance or affluence, for they are a divine election and a merciful outpouring, which He bestows upon the souls of those prepared for them and the spirits of those who receive them.

And (al-sukhriyy), with a dammah, is a relative noun derived from (al-sukhrah), on the pattern of (ghurfah), and it means employment and compulsion to work.

﴿And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ That is, prophethood is better than what they gather of the perishing trash; and the great one is he who is given it and attains it, namely the Prophet ﷺ, not he who has gained much of the beloved desires.

Then the Exalted indicated the lowliness of this world in His sight, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verses 33–35:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[33–35] ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways by which they could ascend, and doors for their houses and couches on which they could recline, and ornaments of gold. But all that would be nothing but the enjoyment of worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for those who are conscious of Him.﴾

﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾ i.e., agreed upon disbelief in God, Exalted is He; that is, were it not for the aversion to that: ﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ i.e., to multiply blessings upon them, despite their disbelief in the Bestower, so that they would increase in punishment: ﴿for their houses﴾ is a substitution for ﴿for those who﴾ (i.e., for them); ﴿silver ceilings﴾ with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, and also with a damma on both, as a plural; ﴿of silver, and stairways﴾ i.e., ascents of silver: ﴿by which they could ascend﴾ i.e., climb. ﴿And doors for their houses﴾ [43:34] i.e., of silver: ﴿and couches﴾ [43:34] i.e., of silver: ﴿on which they could recline﴾ [43:34]. ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾ [43:35] i.e., and We would have made for them along with that ornaments, i.e., adornment of gold and jewels above the silver. Then He indicated that there is no indication in that of their superiority, by His words: ﴿But all that would be nothing but the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ [43:35], i.e., all these things that were mentioned, of silver ceilings, stairways, doors, couches of silver, and ornaments, are nothing but enjoyment which the people of the world enjoy in the world. ﴿And the Hereafter with your Lord is for those who are conscious of Him﴾ [43:35], i.e., the abode of the Hereafter and its splendour are with your Lord for those who are conscious of God, that is, those who fear God and fear His punishment, strive in His obedience and beware of His disobedience, exclusively and not others. Al-Mahayimi said: That is, there is no special distinction in that enjoyment, such that its absence would indicate the absence of the station of prophethood; rather, what its absence indicates is the absence of prophethood, which is piety. Prophethood is only for one whose piety is complete, whether or not he possesses such things. Worldly adornment is more fitting for the disbelievers, because it stirs up the darkness of desires that prevent seeing the truth, so that its possessor becomes blind. End.

Note:

What we have presented, that the meaning of ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾ is under the assumption of (were it not for the aversion to that), and that the meaning of their being one community is their gathering upon one matter, which is disbelief, i.e., that the aversion to gathering upon disbelief is what prevents giving the disbeliever enjoyment of these things in the manner mentioned — this is what the exegetes stated. It was objected to this: when He did not extend provision to the disbelievers, due to the trial that extending it to them would lead to, namely that people would all converge upon disbelief out of their love of the world and their greed for it, why not extend it to the Muslims so that people would converge upon Islam? It was answered that extending it to them is also a corruption, because of what it leads to, namely entering Islam for the sake of worldly gain. Entering religion for the sake of worldly gain is the religion of the hypocrites. So the wisdom in what He arranged was that He placed among both groups the rich and the poor, with poverty predominating over wealth. This is what al-Zamakhshari said.

In my view, there is no need to assume the aversion, and the meaning of the verse is other than what they stated. The meaning is: Were it not that they would be created to be one community, mutually supporting, cooperating, and united, with what sustains their life like a single body, We would have given people the mentioned adornments and ornaments, since that falls within complete power; but that would nullify wisdom and ruin the order of existence. He expressed "mankind" as "those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful" out of consideration for the majority, who are the disbelievers, for they are the ones who covered the face of the earth and filled its surface; and to belittle the worth of the world and diminish its standing, by giving it to the one who is lowest in rank and most base in worth.

The summary of the meaning: that their creation as one community, civilized by nature, prevents the spreading of the world over all of them. This is the consistent meaning of (lawla): that what follows it is always an obstacle to its response; for this reason they say: "a particle of non-existence for the existence of something."

So the meaning is not as they stated at all, as becomes clear to whoever examines carefully. In sum, this verse is a completion of what precedes it, in answer to those who supposed that worldly grandeur entails prophethood.

Thus He, exalted is He, explained His wisdom in the disparity among creation in the first verse, namely subjugation. In the second, the baseness of the world in His sight, and that were it not for subjugation He would have given it to the lowest of creation and the furthest from Him, as an exaggeration in informing of its insignificance. This is the confirmation of what is reported: that the world does not weigh with God the wing of a gnat, and that what is with Him is better and more lasting.

In my view, there is no need to assume the aversion, and the meaning of the verse is other than what they stated. The meaning is: Were it not that they would be created to be one community, mutually supporting, cooperating, and united, with what sustains their life like a single body, We would have given people the mentioned adornments and ornaments, since that falls within complete power; but that would nullify wisdom and ruin the order of existence. He expressed "mankind" as "those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful" out of consideration for the majority, who are the disbelievers, for they are the ones who covered the face of the earth and filled its surface; and to belittle the worth of the world and diminish its standing, by giving it to the one who is lowest in rank and most base in worth.

The summary of the meaning: that their creation as one community, civilized by nature, prevents the spreading of the world over all of them. This is the consistent meaning of (lawla): that what follows it is always an obstacle to its response; for this reason they say: "a particle of non-existence for the existence of something."

So the meaning is not as they stated at all, as becomes clear to whoever examines carefully. In sum, this verse is a completion of what precedes it, in answer to those who supposed that worldly grandeur entails prophethood.

Thus He, exalted is He, explained His wisdom in the disparity among creation in the first verse, namely subjugation. In the second, the baseness of the world in His sight, and that were it not for subjugation He would have given it to the lowest of creation and the furthest from Him, as an exaggeration in informing of its insignificance. This is the confirmation of what is reported: that the world does not weigh with God the wing of a gnat, and that what is with Him is better and more lasting.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[36] ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.﴾

﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ means: who turns away from it, not fearing His might and not dreading His punishment. ﴿We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾ means: We make for him a devil who misleads him and constantly leads him astray from the straight path, because he accompanies him.

Al-Qashani said: It is read as (يُعْشُ), with a damma on the shin and also with a fatha. The difference is that عَشا is used when one looks with the vision of one who is dazzled, either due to an obstacle or deliberately, without any defect in his sight. And عَشِيَ is used when his sight is weakened. According to the first reading, the meaning is: whoever has a pure disposition and a sound natural capacity for comprehending the remembrance of the Most Merciful, that is, the Qur'an sent down from Him, and understands its meaning and knows that it is true, yet turns blindly away from it out of worldly purpose, insolent envy, or jealousy; or he does not understand it and does not know its reality, because he is veiled by natural coverings and preoccupied with sensory pleasures, or because he is deceived by his religion and the belief he holds and his false creed. ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾, a jinn, who misleads him by enticing and adorning for him the pleasures in which he is immersed and the ornaments he covets, or by the doubts and falsehoods that mislead him regarding the religion he has adopted by his own desire; or a human devil who misleads him, shares his affair, resembles him in his path, and keeps him far from the truth. According to the second reading, the meaning is: whoever has a corrupted capacity from the outset, and is wretched from eternity, in that his heart is incapable of perceiving the realities of the remembrance and falls short of understanding its meaning: ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾ from his own self or his kind, who accompanies him in his error and misguidance. End of quotation.

(p-٥٢٧٣) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[37] ﴿And indeed, they bar them from the way, while they think that they are guided.﴾

﴿And indeed, they bar them from the way﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, indeed the devils bar those who turn away from the remembrance of God from the way of truth. They adorn error for them and make faith in God and acting in obedience to Him hateful to them. ﴿while they think that they are guided﴾ That is, these polytheists think, because of the devils' adornment of what they are upon for them, that they are upon what is right and guidance.

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he will say: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! How wretched a companion!"﴾

﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾: that is, the one who turns away (al-'Ashi). ﴿He will say﴾: that is, to his devil: ﴿"Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts"﴾: that is, the distance between the east and the west. He gave precedence to the east over the west and then used the dual. It was also said that what is meant is the two easts of summer and winter, and the intended sense is "of the two wests," so it was abbreviated.

﴿How wretched a companion!﴾ Al-Qashani said: That is, when Our punishment, which is bound to his beliefs and deeds, and the torment deserved by his doctrine and religion, has come upon him, he wishes for the utmost distance between himself and his devil, who misguided him from the truth and adorned for him what brought him into punishment. He feels estranged from his companion and blames him, because the natural bond is absent, or because the ties between them have been cut by the corruption of the bodily faculties.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾

Al-Qashani said: That is, wishing will not benefit you at the time the punishment descends and the deserved retribution becomes due, once your wrongdoing in the world is established and confirmed, its consequence is made clear, and its state is uncovered. This is because you share in the punishment by sharing in its cause. (p-٥٢٧٤) Or: your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you in lessening its severity and its pain. That is, just as those who fall into a difficult matter are helped by others in bearing its burdens, this sharing does not help you in that way.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿Can you then make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾

﴿Can you then make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾ This is a rhetorical denial expressing wonder at the idea that he would be the one able to guide them. He means that none can do so with respect to them except Allah alone, exalted is He. The expression of them as deaf, blind and astray has been repeated in the Revelation, for there is no more comprehensive description of their condition, nor any more eloquent: they have been deprived of hearing the proofs and guidance of Allah, like the deaf, and of seeing the signs of Allah and taking lesson from them, like the blind; and [they have lost] the path, like the lost wanderer who is bewildered.

The commentary on the words of His Exalted saying:

[41] ﴿So whether We take you away, indeed We will take vengeance upon them﴾.

﴿Whether We take you away﴾: that is, We take you in death before We grant you victory over them. ﴿Indeed We will take vengeance upon them﴾: that is, with the punishment of the Hereafter.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted, saying:

[42] ﴿Or We will show you that which We have promised them, for indeed We are Able over them.﴾

﴿Or We will show you that which We have promised them, for indeed We are Able over them.﴾ This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.﴾ [Ghafir: 77]. And in His expressing it with "promise" — while He does not break the appointment — is an indication that it is what will certainly occur. And so it was: not one of their chieftains escaped, except those who fortified themselves with faith.

(p-5275)The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[43] ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are upon a straight path.﴾

﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are upon a straight path.﴾ means: the religion of Allah which He commanded, and it is Islam, for it is perfectly upright in every respect. Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: This is a consolation for him (ﷺ) and a command to his community, or to him, to persist in holding fast. The fa' (so) is the response to an implied condition, meaning: if one of these two (matters) is certain to occur, then hold fast to it.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[44] ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people; and you will be questioned.﴾

﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people⁠﴾: that is, what has been revealed to you is indeed an honour for you and for your people of Quraysh, because of what He has singled them out with, namely its descent in their tongue. Or the intended meaning of "your people" is your followers; that is, it is an exaltation of your rank and the rank of your community, because of what He has given them through it of knowledge, virtues, distinctions, and laws suited to all conditions and times. It is also permissible that "the reminder" be understood as admonition. ﴿And you will be questioned﴾: that is, about what you did concerning it, regarding your compliance with His commands and your abstention from His prohibitions.

The discussion of the Lord's words:

[45] ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾

﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ That is: Did We ever decree the worship of idols? And did it come in any of their creeds (milal)? Al-Qadi said: What is intended by this is to call as witness the consensus of the prophets upon monotheism (tawhid), and to indicate that it is not an innovation (bid'ah) that he has invented, so that he would be denied and opposed for it. End of quotation.

Those whom the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to ask are the believers among the People of the Two Books: the Torah and the Gospel. The speech therefore contains an implied elision (taqdir mudaf): that is, "the believing communities of them." Or it may be that their being asked is treated as being in the position of asking their prophets, since they only inform him about the books of the messengers; so when he asks them, it is as though he had asked the prophets.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[46] ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, so he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾

﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾, i.e., those confirming him, ﴿to Pharaoh﴾ so that he would forbid him from enslaving [people] (al-istib'ad), ﴿and his chiefs﴾, i.e., so that he would forbid them from worshipping him (al-ta'abbud lahu), ﴿so he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds"﴾, i.e., he made clear that none other than Him, exalted is He, deserves worship, and that no one besides Him has the right to enslavement, because it is the right of absolute Lordship (al-rububiyyah al-mutlaqah).

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[47] ﴿So when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them.﴾

﴿So when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them.﴾ When he came to them with the proofs for monotheism and the disavowal of polytheism, behold, Pharaoh and his people laughed. Meaning: just as your people mock the signs and lessons you have brought them. This is a consolation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His Prophet (ﷺ), regarding what he was encountering from the polytheists of his people, and an informing from Him that his people, being of the people of polytheism, will be no different from the other nations who followed their path in disbelief in Allah and denial of His messengers. It is also an exhortation from Him to His Prophet (ﷺ) to follow their example by being patient with them, in the manner of the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulu al-'Azm). And it is an informing from Him to him that the end of their rebellion is destruction and ruin, as was His custom with those who rebelled against their messengers before him, and His granting him victory over them and elevating his cause, like what was done to Musa (peace be upon him) and his people who believed in him, through their being made victorious over Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs. Ibn Jarir conveyed this.

(p-5277) Then he pointed out that the cause of the mockery was none other than obstinacy, not any deficiency in the signs, by His saying:

[56, 58] ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for the later ones.﴾ ﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it.﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57) ﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not cite it to you except for disputation. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58)

﴿So We made them a precedent﴾, meaning a proof for those who perished after them, ﴿and an example﴾, meaning a lesson, ﴿for the later ones﴾, meaning those who were saved.

﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57), meaning in his being like Adam, as the verse indicates: ﴿Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ (Al 'Imran: 59). The meaning is that, given what is established between his being described as a created servant of God, blessed with prophethood, that worshipping him is disbelief, and calling upon him is polytheism, since God has not permitted the worship of anything other than Him. ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57), meaning from his cited example and his clarified description, ﴿turn away﴾, meaning they turn aside and do not heed.

﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58). By "our gods" they mean the angels whom they worshipped, asserting that they are the daughters of God, the Exalted, as was mentioned of them at the beginning of the surah (p. 5279). The meaning is that they are better than Jesus and more excellent, because they belong to the Exalted Assembly and the most lofty kind. So if it is permissible to worship the less excellent, who is Jesus, then it is all the more so to worship the more excellent, who are the angels. It is as though they agree on their polytheism through sound premises, and build upon their adherence to it clear analogies, but they were heedless, due to their ignorance, of the invalidity of both the analogized and that to which it is analogized, and that the decisive proof has established the invalidity of worshipping other than God, the Exalted, and the impossibility of procreation in His exalted Essence.

When guidance has become clear, nothing remains beyond it but error and the stirring up of strife through disputation, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿They did not cite it to you except for disputation﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58), meaning they did not put forward this statement to you except for the sake of argument and contention, not out of conviction, since its invalidity is evident. ﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58), meaning they are intensely contentious in falsehood, through deception and confusion. In a hadith: "No people went astray after guidance they had been upon except that they were given disputation." What we have stated in the interpretation of this verse is the clear and evident meaning, as indicated by the siyaq (the context of the verse) and the sibaq (the preceding context). So compare it with what others have related, and be fair.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[56, 58] ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for the later ones.﴾ ﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it.﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57) ﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not cite it to you except for disputation. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58)

﴿So We made them a precedent﴾, meaning a proof for those who perished after them, ﴿and an example﴾, meaning a lesson, ﴿for the later ones﴾, meaning those who were saved.

﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57), meaning in his being like Adam, as the verse indicates: ﴿Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ (Al 'Imran: 59). The meaning is that, given what is established between his being described as a created servant of God, blessed with prophethood, that worshipping him is disbelief, and calling upon him is polytheism, since God has not permitted the worship of anything other than Him. ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 57), meaning from his cited example and his clarified description, ﴿turn away﴾, meaning they turn aside and do not heed.

﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 58). By "our gods" they mean the angels whom they worshipped, asserting that they are the daughters of God, the Exalted, as was mentioned of them at the beginning of the surah (p. 5279). What we have stated in the interpretation of this verse is the clear and evident meaning, as indicated by the siyaq (the context of the verse) and the sibaq (the preceding context). So compare it with what others have related, and be fair.

[59] ﴿He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example (mathal) for the Children of Israel.﴾

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[60] ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you angels replacing you on the earth, succeeding one another.﴾

﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you﴾ i.e., instead of you: ﴿angels on the earth, succeeding one another﴾, i.e., they would be in your place. This is a warning to them that they are in the grip of His will regarding their destruction and the replacement of them with one better than them.

(p-٥٢٨١) On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[63, 64] ﴿When Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 64].

﴿When Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ"﴾ That is, of the rulings of the Torah and others, such as the disagreement of the Jews concerning the Resurrection, due to its not being explicit in their books. A similar statement has come in the verse: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50]. He lifted from the Jews some of the burden of the Torah and the shackles of the Law (al-namus), as he did regarding the Sabbath, lessening the severity of its ruling.

Some of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun) said: He did not say "to make clear to you all that about which you differ," because he did not do that. Rather, he left the explanation of many matters, such as the corruption that entered most of their books, concerning the Paraclete (Muhammad ﷺ) who would come after him, owing to the people of his time not being prepared to accept everything from him. As he himself said in the Gospel of John, in chapter sixteen. And especially if he addressed the attack upon their books, which are their sole capital and the heritage of their forefathers; had he done so, many of them would have doubted him and denied him, and only a few or rare ones would have followed him, and the benefit of his mission, which we have explained in the text, would be lost, and that is the purpose for which he was sent.

As for the words of Allah, exalted is He, quoting him: ﴿and confirming what is before me of the Torah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50], the meaning of such an expression is that by his coming, peace be upon him, the prophecies of the Torah concerning him were fulfilled, and through him they were proven true and correct. The word "Torah" is applied to the Old Testament; so the meaning is that the coming of Jesus was in accordance with what the prophets had foretold about him beforehand. Had it not been for him, those prophecies would not have been true, for they apply to none but him. It is not meant that (p-٥٢٨٢) Jesus affirms everything in the Torah, as the Christians now imagine from verses like this one. Otherwise, he would not have said immediately afterward: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50]. So reflect upon this, and do not be like those who speak about what they do not know, and interpret what they do not understand. End of his words. And it is very sound.

[65] ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who did wrong from the punishment of a painful day.﴾

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[66, 67] ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?﴾ ﴿On that Day, friends will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

[p. 5283] ﴿Do they await﴾: i.e., Quraysh. ﴿anything but the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly while they are unaware﴾. ﴿On that Day, friends﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]: i.e., those who befriend one another in disobedience, corruption, and turning away from the truth. ﴿will be enemies to one another﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]: i.e., hostile, each disowning his companion. ﴿except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]: i.e., those who are sincere friends in obedience to Allah and in love for Him.

Al-Qashani said: Friendship (khullah) is either good (khayriyyah) or not. Good friendship is either in Allah or for Allah and His love. Non-good friendship has as its cause either carnal pleasure or intellectual benefit.

The first category is spiritual, essential love, based on the affinity of souls in pre-eternity, concerning which it was said: "The souls are like conscripted troops; those that recognized one another in them become familiar, and those that did not recognize one another in them differ." So when they emerge in this world, turn toward the Truth, and are renewed from the sources of impurity, when they meet they recognize one another, and when they recognize one another they love one another, because of their original kinship, their agreement in direction and path, their similarity in conduct and disposition, and their detachment from corrupt aims and from the accidental attributes that are the cause of enmity.

Each of them benefits from the other in his conduct and his knowledge, delights in meeting him, is purified by his purity, and they cooperate in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. This is perfect and real friendship, which never ceases, like the love of the prophets, the chosen ones, the saints, and the martyrs.

The second category is the love of the heart, based on the affinity of qualities, morals, and virtuous conduct, and arising from sound beliefs and righteous deeds, like the love of the righteous and the pious for one another, the love of the gnostics and the saints for them, and the love of the prophets for their communities.

The third category is carnal love, based on sensory pleasures and particular accidental attributes, like the love of spouses for mere desire, and the love of the wicked and the sinners who cooperate in obtaining desires and seizing wealth.

The fourth category is intellectual love, based on facilitating the means of livelihood and easing worldly interests, like the love of merchants and craftsmen, and the love of the benefactor for the one who benefits from him. Everything that is based on a perishable aim and a passing cause vanishes with the vanishing of that cause, and upon its loss it turns into enmity, because each of the lovers expects from his companion the familiar pleasure and the customary benefit, and when the cause ceases he withholds them. [p. 5284]

Since the predominant concern of the people of knowledge is one of the last two categories, He spoke in absolute terms and said: ﴿On that Day, friends will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67], because the means of connection between them will be cut off, the bodily instruments will be absent from them, sensory pleasure and physical benefit will be impossible, and these will turn into regrets, pains, harm, and loss. Pleasures and desires will have vanished, and punishments and consequences will remain, so each one abhors and hates his companion, because he sees the torment upon him, from him and because of him.

Then He excepted the righteous who partake of the two remaining categories, because of their rarity, as He said: ﴿and few are they﴾ [Sad: 24], and ﴿and few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba': 13]. By my life, the first category is rarer than the red sulphur (al-kibrit al-ahmar, the legendary elixir). These are the perfect in piety, who reach its utmost limit and attain all its ranks. Next to them is the second category. Both categories share in seeking the good pleasure of Allah, seeking His reward, and avoiding His wrath and His punishment. Glorified is He, He attributed them to Himself by His saying:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 43, verses 71–72:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[71, 72] ﴿Therein will be passed around to them dishes of gold and cups, and therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally.﴾ ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72].

﴿Therein will be passed around to them dishes of gold and cups﴾ Al-sihaf (dishes) is the plural of (safha), which is a vessel for eating. Al-akwab (cups) is the plural of (kub), which is that from which one drinks, like a jug (kuz), except that the kub is one that has no handle (urwa). Al-Shihab said: the urwa is that by which something is held, and it is called an ear (udhun). For this reason, one who composed a riddle about it said:

"And one with an ear that has no hearing, who has a heart without a heart.
When he takes control over a lover, say whatever you wish about the lover."

Among the subtle points here is what has been said: since vessels for food are usually more numerous than vessels for drink, the first was given the plural of abundance (jam' kathra) and the second the plural of paucity (jam' qilla).

﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in﴾ meaning, by seeing it. ﴿And you will abide therein eternally.﴾ ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72] meaning: of good deeds and righteous works. He has likened what they deserved by their good deeds, of the Paradise and its enduring bliss that remains for them, to what a person leaves behind for his heirs of properties and provisions. It entails also the comparison of the deed itself to the one who bequeaths (in the form of the active participle), so it is a metaphor of a subsequent kind (isti'ara tab'iyya), or an allegorical metaphor (tamthiliyya).

Among the subtle points here is what has been said: since vessels for food are usually more numerous than vessels for drink, the first was given the plural of abundance (jam' kathra) and the second the plural of paucity (jam' qilla).

﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in﴾ meaning, by seeing it. ﴿And you will abide therein eternally.﴾ ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72] meaning: of good deeds and righteous works. He has likened what they deserved by their good deeds, of the Paradise and its enduring bliss that remains for them, to what a person leaves behind for his heirs of properties and provisions. It entails also the comparison of the deed itself to the one who bequeaths (in the form of the active participle), so it is a metaphor of a subsequent kind (isti'ara tab'iyya), or an allegorical metaphor (tamthiliyya).

(p-5286) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His, may He be exalted, Words:

[73] ﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, of which you will eat.﴾

﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, of which you will eat.﴾ That is: whatever you desire. The "min" (of) in "minhā" is either for the beginning (ibtidā'iyyah) or for partition (tab'īḍiyyah). It is preferred, given that it indicates the abundance of blessings, that they are neither cut off nor prevented, and that they are always adorned with fruits, laden with them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verses 74–75:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[74, 75] ﴿Indeed, the criminals will abide in the punishment of Hell.﴾ ﴿It will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it in despair.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 75].

﴿Indeed, the criminals﴾ means: those who committed disbelief (kufr) and sins (ma'asi) in the worldly life. ﴿will abide in the punishment of Hell﴾ ﴿It will not be lightened for them﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 75], meaning: it will not be eased or reduced. ﴿and they will be in it in despair﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 75], meaning: they will be submissive and despairing (mustaslimun ya'isun).

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[76] ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were themselves the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And We did not wrong them﴾, i.e., by this punishment. ﴿But they were themselves the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., by their disbelief in Allah and their denial of His Oneness.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verses 77–78:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[77, 78] ﴿They will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ ﴿We had certainly brought you the truth, but most of you were averse to the truth.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 78].

﴿And they will call﴾, that is, after their entry into Jahannam (Hell): ﴿"O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us"﴾, that is, let Him cause us to die. That is: ask Him to do that for us. They wish for the cessation of the senses and the absence of perception, because of the severity of the pain from the physical torment (p-5287). ﴿He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ That is, you will abide: ﴿"We had certainly brought you the truth, but most of you were averse to the truth."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 78], that is, you do not accept it and you recoil from it. He expressed it with "most" (bi-l-akthar) because among the followers there are those who disbelieve through blind imitation (taqlid).

A subtle point:

Al-Qashani said: The keeper of the Fire was named (Malik) because of his specific association with those who possessed the world and preferred it, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for he who transgressed﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 37] ﴿and preferred the life of this world﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 38] ﴿then indeed Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 39]. Just as the keeper of Paradise was named (Ridwan) because of his specific association with those with whom Allah is pleased and who are pleased with Him.

The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil, the deeper meaning or explanation) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[79] ﴿Or have they devised a plan? Then it is We who are the devisers.﴾

﴿Or have they devised a plan? Then it is We who are the devisers.﴾ That is: Or have the polytheists of Makkah devised a plan and firmly settled it, plotting by it against the truth that has come to them? Then We are the ones who firmly settle for them what will disgrace and humiliate them, of punishment. Like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they intend a scheme? But those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be ensnared by the scheme.﴾ [al-Tur: 42]

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[80] ﴿Do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes indeed, and Our messengers are with them, writing down.﴾

﴿Do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk?﴾ That is: what they conceal of their secret consultations, with which they plot; so We will not requite them for it, since it is hidden from Us. ﴿Yes indeed﴾ — that is, We hear both of them and are aware of them. ﴿And Our messengers﴾ — meaning the guardian angels — ﴿are with them, writing down﴾ — that is, whatever they have spoken and uttered of words.

Then He pointed to refuting their falsehood in claiming that the angels are the daughters of Allah, exalted is He, thereby concluding the surah with what it began with, what the rhetoricians call (radd al-ʿajuz ʿala al-ṣadr) (returning the end to the beginning). So He, glorified is He, said:

(p-5288) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[81] ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾

﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.﴾ That is: for that son. The "firstness" is relative to those addressed, not to those who came before them. Al-Shihab said: "Had it been left on its general sense, with the intention of expressing eagerness and haste, it would be permissible." End of quote.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[82] ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾

﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ This is a negation of the consequent (al-tali; the conclusion of a conditional). The consequent is the worship of the child, i.e., "I would be the first of the worshippers." The meaning is: I affirm His oneness and exalt Him, exalted is He, above what they ascribe to Him of being similar to anything. Because He is the Lord and the Creator of all bodies, He is not of their kind. Thus this indicates the negation of a child by the demonstrative method (al-burhani).

As for its indication of the second point: if His saying "Glory be to the Lord of the heavens" and so on is taken as the speech of God, exalted is He, and not the speech of the Messenger, then the meaning is: "Glorify the Lord of the heavens above what they ascribe to Him." It is then a negation of the antecedent (al-muqaddam), and the conditional linking of the Messenger's worship is of the type of conditioning on something impossible. What is conditioned on a condition, when that condition is absent, is established by the indication of the implicit meaning (dalalat al-mafhum), which is more eloquent according to the scholars of rhetoric (ulama al-bayan) than the indication of the explicit meaning (dalalat al-manṭuq). As He said in dismissing the possibility of seeing Him:

﴿But if it remains in its place, then you will see Me﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. End of quotation.

Discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[83] ﴿So leave them to plunge into their vain talk and to play, until they encounter their Day which they are promised.﴾

﴿So leave them to plunge (yakhūḍū)﴾ meaning: in their falsehood. ﴿And to play (yalʿabū)﴾ meaning: in their worldly life. ﴿Until they encounter their Day which they are promised.﴾ (p-5289) Ibn Jarir said: That is the day on which Allah will cause them to burn in Hell for their fabrication against Him, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[84] ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ means: the one worshipped in both, without partner. ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ means: in His management of His creation, and His subjecting them to what He wills for their benefit.

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[85–86] ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ ﴿Those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession, except one who testifies to the truth while they know.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 86]

﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ ﴿Those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 86], i.e., intercession for them with God, just as they claimed that their equals (andad) are intercessors. ﴿except one who testifies to the truth while they know﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 86], i.e., one who believes in God and affirms His oneness, while they know the reality of His oneness; that is, they declared Him one and sincerely devoted themselves to Him with knowledge and certainty, as in His words: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 28]. Ibn Kathir said: "This is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but whoever testifies to the truth with insight and knowledge, his intercession will benefit him with Him, by His permission for him." Ended.

(p-5290) Caution:

Al-Shihab said: The jurists have used this verse as evidence that testimony is only valid when it is based on knowledge, and that it is permissible even if the witness did not witness it.

In (al-Iklil), al-Kiya said: The words of the Exalted, ﴿except one who testifies to the truth while they know﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 86], indicate two meanings. The first: that testimony to the truth is not beneficial except with knowledge, and that imitation (taqlid) does not suffice in the absence of knowledge of the soundness of the statement. The second: that the condition for testimonies in rights and other matters is that the witness be knowledgeable of them.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[87] ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾

﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ meaning: He created us, because denial of this is impossible owing to its extreme clarity. ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾ meaning: they are diverted from worshipping Him to worshipping other than Him.

[88] ﴿And [the Messenger's] saying: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe."﴾

﴿And his saying﴾ means: the saying of Muhammad, may God's blessings be upon him (ﷺ), complaining to his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, about his people who denied him and about what he suffered from them: ﴿"O my Lord, these"﴾, that is, those whom You commanded me to warn and whom You sent me to in order to call them to You: ﴿"are a people who do not believe"﴾, that is, in tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), in the prophethood, and in the Last Day. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 43, verse 89:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[89] ﴿So turn away from them and say, "Peace." But they will soon know.﴾

(p-5291) ﴿So turn away﴾, i.e., avoid them. ﴿from them and say, "Peace"﴾, i.e., for you, or upon you, or my affair is peace; that is, a parting of ways. It is thus a peace of departure, not a greeting (tahiyyah).

Al-Razi said: Some people have used this verse as evidence that it is permissible to give the greeting of peace to a disbeliever. Then he said: If this inference is valid, it requires restricting oneself to the bare utterance "Peace" (salam), and saying to a believer "Peace be upon you." The intended purpose is to draw attention to the greeting that is mentioned for the Muslim and the disbeliever alike. End of quote.

This is open to scrutiny, because it is a rigid adherence to the mere outward meaning here and a neglect of its parallels, such as the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him, to his father: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ [Maryam: 47], and the verse ﴿Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant﴾ [al-Qasas: 55]. Most scholars hold that the predicate here is omitted, i.e., "upon you," and what is implied is like what is stated, and what is omitted for a reason is like what is present. So the correct view is that the peace here is one of parting. And God knows best.

﴿But they will soon know﴾, i.e., the truth of what you were sent with, through the ascendancy of the truth and the vanishing of falsehood.

Note:

It has been read as "wa-qīlahu" in the accusative, in coordination with "sirrahum wa-najwahum" (their secret and their private talk). This reading has been deemed weak because of the intervening separation between the conjoined and the element it is conjoined to, by something that is not suitably parenthetical. Or it is in coordination with the locus of "al-sa'ah" (the Hour), since it is in an accusative locus, being a verbal noun governed by its object; or by supposing a verb: i.e., "and he said his saying."

It has been read in the genitive, in coordination with "al-sa'ah," or the waw is for swearing an oath, with the response omitted; i.e., "I will surely do to them what I intend," or it is stated, and it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, these are a people who do not believe﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88].

It has been read in the nominative, in coordination with "'ilm al-sa'ah" (knowledge of the Hour), with a noun supplied: i.e., "and with Him is the knowledge of his saying." Or it is nominative as the subject, and the clause "O my Lord" etc. is the predicate. Or the predicate is omitted: i.e., "and his saying is such-and-such, heard or accepted." In the marginal notes (al-Hawashi) there are dialectical figurative points; increase your knowledge by consulting them.
